chunks: From him, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a person performing i'tikaf (spiritual retreat) who had intercourse with his wife. He said: Upon him is what is upon the one who deliberately broke his fast for a day in the month of Ramadan: freeing a slave, or fasting two consecutive months, or feeding sixty poor people.
ai.seo_question: What is the penalty for sexual intercourse during i'tikaf?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-istibsar clarifies that sexual intercourse during i'tikaf incurs the same expiation (kaffarah) as breaking the Ramadan fast deliberately, reflecting the juristic view that the sanctity of the retreat is violated similarly to the sanctity of the fasting month. The ruling underscores the continuity of ritual purity obligations in Shia fiqh, linking the specific act of intimacy to the broader framework of kaffarah found in Surah Al-Baqarah. It highlights the scholarly consensus on the equivalence of penalties for major ritual breaches in these contexts.
